value.name: sleeps well enough
value.description: She sleeps better than she has since the Serrano file arrived, though not perfectly.
evidence: She did not, that night, sleep badly.
She slept the way she had used to sleep before the Serrano file had come into her office

value.name: wakes at six
value.description: She wakes up at six in the morning.

value.name: makes morning coffee
value.description: She prepares coffee as part of her morning routine.

value.name: prepares for new client intake
value.description: At her kitchen table, she begins organizing notes for a new client scheduled to come in at nine.
evidence: She sat at her kitchen table with a fresh pad of paper and a fresh pen and she wrote, at the top, the name of a new client, whose intake was scheduled for nine

value.name: notes difficult family warning
value.description: She records that the new client's family has been described as difficult and marks the word for emphasis.
evidence: whose family, she had been told by the referring attorney, was difficult, and she underlined the word *difficult*
and then, after a moment, crossed out the underline

value.name: reframes difficult families
value.description: She reflects that difficult estates often use that label to intimidate handlers and that the hardest-looking families may simply be afraid.
evidence: she had learned, over the last six weeks, that *difficult* was a word that estates threw at the people who handled them in order to scare them away from doing the work properly
and that the families who looked the most difficult from the outside were often the families who, on the inside, were most afraid that no one would help them tell the truth

value.name: walks to the office
value.description: She leaves home and goes to her office.
evidence: She drank her coffee. She walked to the office.

value.name: opens new file
value.description: She opens the new case file at the office.

value.name: files Serrano codicil
value.description: The original codicil is filed with the Register of Wills, copied into Asha's closed-estates binder, and shelved in her office.
evidence: The codicil, in its original form, with Rosa's signature on it as a witness and Mrs. Serrano's signature on it in the careful slow handwriting of a woman who had taken her time, was filed in the Register of Wills office in Philadelphia and assigned a number
and a copy of it was placed in the binder Asha kept for closed estates, and the binder was placed on a shelf in her office
value.location_hint: Register of Wills office in Philadelphia / Asha's office
